sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Gram Swaraj (Village Self-Reliance)**: Ultimate political and economic decentralization where every village is a self-contained republic producing its own food, clothing, and basic necessities.
• **Trusteeship**: Economic philosophy where wealthy individuals do not own property absolutely but hold it in trust for society, using excess wealth for community welfare.
• **Swadeshi & Charkha**: Emphasizes the use of locally produced goods and the spinning wheel as symbols of economic independence, dignity of labor, and eradication of rural unemployment.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Maximization of moral and material progress without violence, exploitation, or ecological degradation.

Economic restraint where accumulation of excess wealth is discouraged to maintain social equity and ecological balance.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Rural Hinterlands & Artisan Clusters**: Concentrated across handloom and handicraft clusters in states like Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, and Rajasthan.
• **Driving Advantages**: Utilization of traditional indigenous skill sets, low capital investment, high female workforce participation, and utilization of locally available raw materials.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Low productivity, obsolete technology, fragmented supply chains, market access deficits, and competition from cheap machine-made goods.
• **Policy Interventions**: SFURTI scheme for traditional industries, PMEGP for employment generation, digital marketing integration, and Geographical Indication (GI) tagging.

items.title: Mnemonic for Gandhian Economic Pillars
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'STARS' (Swadeshi, Trusteeship, Antyodaya, Rural self-sufficiency, Sarvodaya).
• **Decoded Meaning**: S-Swadeshi, T-Trusteeship, A-Antyodaya, R-Rural focus, S-Sarvodaya.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly validates options when identifying core pillars of Gandhian economic thought in matching-type questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Gandhi rejected *unbridled industrialization* but accepted *machinery that lightened human labor* (e.g., Singer sewing machine) without displacing human employment.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently poses statements claiming Gandhi was entirely against all machinery and modern technology. Correction: Gandhi opposed machinery that enslaved labor or caused mass unemployment, but welcomed tools that enhanced human efficiency and reduced drudgery.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 (Inclusive Growth & Decentralization), quote Gandhian trusteeship and Gram Swaraj as indigenous models for corporate social responsibility (CSR) and modern sustainable local governance.

keyTakeaways: Gandhian economic strategy centers on Gram Swaraj, decentralization, and moral upliftment via Sarvodaya.
Trusteeship and Swadeshi serve as ethical and practical tools against wealth concentration and exploitation.
Modern schemes like KVIC, PMEGP, and SFURTI operationalize Gandhian economic principles in contemporary India.
